narrative.intro: OptumServe Health Services obligated $1.9B in FY2026 to date. OptumServe Health Services received 11 federal awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $170M. OptumServe Health Services obligations are down 26.3% year over year. OptumServe Health Services has trended through prior fiscal years as follows: FY21 $756M, FY22 $874M, FY23 $711M, FY24 $1.6B, FY25 $2.5B, and FY26 $1.9B to date. OptumServe Health Services sells primarily to the Department of Veterans Affairs, which obligated $1.8B so far in FY2026, and also to the Department of Health and Human Services and the Department of Defense, which obligated $11.5M and $11M respectively. OptumServe Health Services revenue in NAICS markets is concentrated in Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) at $1.8B, with smaller work in Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists at $11M, All Other Outpatient Care Centers at $10.8M, and All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services at $719K. The figures reported here are contract obligations except where noted otherwise in award-value tables.

sections.heading: Who are the biggest federal buyers of OptumServe Health Services?
sections.body: Department of Veterans Affairs is the largest buyer, obligating $1.8B to OptumServe Health Services in FY2026 to date. Department of Health and Human Services obligated $11.5M. Department of Defense obligated $11M.

sections.heading: What markets and services drive OptumServe Health Services federal work?
sections.body: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists) is the dominant market at $1.8B. Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists accounted for $11M, All Other Outpatient Care Centers accounted for $10.8M, and All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services accounted for $719K.
